model: Clements mesh in the agentkit.mzi convention with Gaussian splitter-angle errors (shared plus local component). Exact analytic gradient of the global-phase-insensitive infidelity; L-BFGS-B. No geometry, no measured device, no thermal crosstalk, no loss.
hypothesis_under_test: H-C (guide v2 section 39), model part only: in-situ recalibration absorbs correlated fabrication errors of a fs-written mesh down to a fixed transfer error.

strategies.A_ideal_programming: Phases computed for an error-free mesh, applied to the erroneous device.
strategies.B_in_situ: All phases re-optimized on the erroneous device itself (hardware in the loop with exact transfer access), starting from A.
strategies.B_8bit: Phases of B quantized to an 8-bit DAC over 2 pi.
strategies.C_model_based: Phases optimized on a model whose splitter errors were characterized with error of std 0.1 sigma, then applied to the true device.

decision_rule: If the last two criteria pass, H-C is supported in the model at the primary point and remains a candidate headline whose decisive test is physical (T10, T14, T15: measured splitter errors, a measured calibration loop, drift). If either fails, H-C is withdrawn as headline for this error level. Secondary settings, B_8bit and C_model_based are descriptive.
pre_commit_checks: Software smoke test only: analytic gradient versus central differences (N = 5, one random point) and timing of one objective evaluation at N = 8; the ideal device reproduces its target (infidelity below 1e-15). No setting statistic was computed before this commitment.
heldout_policy: Each realization draws a new Haar target and new errors from fixed seeds; nothing is tuned on outcomes.
